text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) said it continues to recommend Swiss chemicals company Clariant AG as a "buy" in a model portfolio, but it advised waiting for details of an acquisition before further purchases.
Earlier Thursday Clariant reported a nine percent increase in group sales in 1996 based on Swiss franc results.
"With an increase of nine percent in Swiss francs, Clariant has grown more quickly than we expected," UBS said.
Clariant also said in December it would acquire a specialty chemicals unit of Germany's Hoechst AG.
"This should boost the long-term profitability of the company," UBS said.
But, it added: "Until the exact details regarding the acquisition and the restructuring are announced in April, we would wait with further buying."

UBS also said that it was raising its earnings estimate slightly. It said that Clariant could see a marked increase in its operating margin to 13 percent from 10 percent currently, but was likely to miss its own goal of a margin of 15 percent.
In its latest review of the company, UBS raised its earnings per share estimate to 55.70 Swiss francs for 1998 from 51.00 in an earlier estimate made in December.
